candidates.title: Rota–Heron–Welsh log-concavity conjecture for matroid characteristic coefficients
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $\mathrm{M}$ be a matroid on a finite set $E$, and write $r+1$ for its rank. Let $\chi_{\mathrm{M}}(\lambda)$ be its characteristic polynomial, and let $w_k(\mathrm{M})$ be the absolute value of the coefficient of $\lambda^{r-k+1}$ in $\chi_{\mathrm{M}}(\lambda)$. **Rota–Heron–Welsh conjecture.** The sequence $w_k(\mathrm{M})$ is log-concave:

$$
w_{k-1}(\mathrm{M})w_{k+1}(\mathrm{M})\leq w_k(\mathrm{M})^2\quad\text{for all }1\leq k\leq r.
$$

In particular, the sequence is unimodal, so for some index $l$,

$$
w_0(\mathrm{M})\leq w_1(\mathrm{M})\leq\cdots\leq w_l(\mathrm{M})\geq\cdots\geq w_r(\mathrm{M})\geq w_{r+1}(\mathrm{M}).
$$

This conjecture extends log-concavity and unimodality questions for chromatic polynomials to arbitrary matroids. The source presents it as an open problem and notes that positivity of the coefficients is used to deduce unimodality from log-concavity.

candidates.title: Infinite log-concavity conjecture for longest-increasing-subsequence polynomials
candidates.literal_statement: For each $n\geq 1$, let $P_n(x)=\sum_k P_{n,k}x^k$, where $P_{n,k}$ is the number of permutations of $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$. A polynomial is **infinitely log-concave** when every polynomial obtained by iterating the log-concavity operator remains log-concave. **Infinite log-concavity conjecture.** $P_n(x)$ is infinitely log-concave for $n\geq 1$. This strengthens the preceding log-concavity proposal for the longest-increasing-subsequence distribution; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

candidates.title: Rational generating functions for grid classes with forest graphs
candidates.literal_statement: Let $M$ be a finite matrix defining a grid class $\operatorname{Grid}(M)$, and let $G(M)$ be the bipartite graph whose vertices represent the rows and columns of $M$, with an edge whenever the corresponding entry of $M$ is nonzero. A generating function is **rational** if it is a quotient of polynomials. **Forest rationality conjecture.** If $G(M)$ is a forest, then $\operatorname{Grid}(M)$ and all its subclasses have rational generating functions. The source describes this as a speculative extension of known results: permutation-matrix grid classes have eventually polynomial enumeration, while star-graph grid classes have rational generating functions. Its resolution is not given in the source.

candidates.title: The random matrix strong convergence conjecture for tensor actions
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{F}_r]\otimes\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{F}_r]$, and let $u$ be an $r$-tuple of free Haar unitaries. For almost every sequence of Haar-random tuples $U^{(N)}\in\mathcal{U}(\mathbb{M}_N(\mathbb{C})^r)$, define $(B\otimes C)\# A=BAC^T$. **The random matrix strong convergence conjecture.** One has

$$
\sup_{R>0}\inf_{F\subset\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{F}_r]\ \mathrm{finite}}\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sup_{\substack{A\in\mathbb{M}_N(\mathbb{C}),\ \|A\|\leq R,\ \|A\|_2\leq1,\\forall P\in F,\ \operatorname{tr}(A^*P(U^N))=0}}\left\|\alpha(U^{(N)}\otimes1_N,1_N\otimes(U^{(N)})^t)\# A\right\|_2
\leq\left\|\alpha(u\otimes1,1\otimes u^{-1})\right\|_{C^*_{\lambda}(\mathbb{F}_r)\otimes_{\min}C^*_{\lambda}(\mathbb{F}_r)}.
$$

The estimate asserts that, after removing finitely many polynomial directions, the random tensor action has the expected limiting norm. The source states that this conjecture has since been resolved by several authors, so its status is solved.

candidates.title: Unimodality conjecture for dominating-set sequences of finite graphs
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite undirected graph on $n$ vertices. A **dominating set** is a set of vertices such that every vertex is either in the set or adjacent to a vertex in the set. For $0\leq j\leq n$, let $d_j(G)$ be the number of dominating sets of $G$ with cardinality $j$. **Unimodality conjecture.** The sequence $d_0(G),\ldots,d_n(G)$ is unimodal: there exists some $0\leq m\leq n$ such that

$$
d_0(G)\leq d_1(G)\leq\cdots\leq d_m(G)\geq d_{m+1}(G)\geq\cdots\geq d_n(G).
$$

The conjecture concerns the shape of dominating-set enumerators, while this paper gives examples showing that dominating-set sequences need not be log-concave. Since log-concavity implies unimodality under the relevant endpoint conditions, disproving log-concavity does not by itself disprove this conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution status for the unimodality claim.

candidates.title: Alikhani–Peng unimodality conjecture for domination sequences
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple undirected graph with vertex set $V(G)$, let $n=|V(G)|$, and let $d_k(G)$ denote the number of dominating sets of $G$ of size $k$. The polynomial

$$
D(G,x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}d_k(G)x^k
$$

records these numbers. **Alikhani–Peng unimodality conjecture.** For every finite graph $G$, the domination sequence $(d_k(G))_{k=0}^{n}$ is unimodal. This conjecture predicts a strong shape constraint on the coefficients of domination polynomials, complementing known structural results from graph operations and studies of their roots. Its general status is unresolved in the supplied source.

candidates.title: Strong Schur log-concavity conjecture for diagonals of the quantum Pascal triangle
candidates.literal_statement:
For $n\geqslant k\geqslant0$, define the quantum binomial by

$$
\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{k}=\frac{[n][n-1]\cdots[n-k+1]}{[k][k-1]\cdots[1]},
$$

where $[n]=(q^{-n}-q^n)/(q^{-1}-q)$ and $[0]=0$. A sequence of Laurent polynomials is strongly Schur log-concave if each difference $a_{n+i}(q)a_n(q)-a_{n+i+1}(q)a_{n-1}(q)$ is centred, unimodal, and has non-negative coefficients. **Quantum Pascal diagonal conjecture.** For all choices of $n\geqslant k\geqslant0$, $\alpha\geqslant-1$, and $\beta\geqslant0$, the diagonal

$$
\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{k},\quad \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-\alpha}{k+\beta},\quad \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-2\alpha}{k+2\beta},\quad \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-3\alpha}{k+3\beta},\quad \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-4\alpha}{k+4\beta},\quad\ldots
$$

of slope $\alpha/\beta$ is strongly Schur log-concave. This is a data-driven conjecture about quantum analogues of Pascal-triangle diagonals; no resolution is supplied in the stated material.

candidates.title: Matrix-analysis inequality implying the tree real-part conjecture
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $\sim_1$ and $\sim_2$ be equivalence relations on $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $P_1$ and $P_2$ be the groups of permutations preserving their respective equivalence classes, and let $A$ be an $n\times n$ Hermitian positive semidefinite matrix. Define

$$
f_{\sim_1,\sim_2}(A)=\sum_{\sigma_1\in P_1}\sum_{\sigma_2\in P_2}\prod_{i=1}^n A_{\sigma_1(i),\sigma_2(i)}.
$$

**Matrix-analysis conjecture.** Under these hypotheses,

$$
\operatorname{Re}(f_{\sim_1,\sim_2}(A))\geq\lvert P_1\cap P_2\rvert\prod_{i=1}^n A_{ii}.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture implies the tree real-part conjecture; no proof or resolution is supplied.
candidates.proof_status: prior public proof claim; not independently certified here

candidates.title: Kantarcı Oğuz's unimodality conjecture for traces of q-deformed matrices
candidates.literal_statement: For a sequence of positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_{2m}$, let $M(a_1,\ldots,a_{2m})$ be the corresponding matrix and call a polynomial $f(q)=\sum_{i=0}^n a_iq^i$ **unimodal** if $a_0\le\cdots\le a_j\ge\cdots\ge a_n$ for some $j$ with $0\le j\le n$. **Kantarcı Oğuz's conjecture.** For any sequence $a_1,\ldots,a_{2m}>0$, the trace $\operatorname{tr}(M(a_1,\ldots,a_{2m}))$ is unimodal except when $(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{2m})=(1,k,1,k)$ or $(k,1,k,1)$ for some $k$; the case $m=2$ is unimodal even in these exceptional cases. This conjecture concerns the coefficient shape of traces related to circular fence posets and would imply corresponding unimodality statements for normalized Jones polynomials of rational links. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

candidates.title: Unimodality conjecture for totally nonnegative Grassmannian cardinalities
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $q=p^r$, where $p$ is an odd prime. For each $n$, consider the sequence

$$
\left(|\operatorname{Gr}_{k,n}^{\geq 0}(\mathbb{F}_q)|\right)_{0\leq k\leq n},
$$

where $\operatorname{Gr}_{k,n}^{\geq 0}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ denotes the totally nonnegative Grassmannian over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. **Unimodality conjecture.** The sequence

$$
\left(|\operatorname{Gr}_{k,n}^{\geq 0}(\mathbb{F}_q)|\right)_{0\leq k\leq n}
$$

is unimodal (log-concave). The sequence is already known to be palindromic, and log-concavity would imply unimodality because all its cardinalities are nonzero; establishing this property is the proposed extension of the corresponding familiar behavior for ordinary Grassmannian cardinalities.

candidates.title: Infinite log-monotonicity conjecture for transposed Boros-Moll sequences
candidates.literal_statement: Let $d_\ell(m)$ be the coefficient of $x^\ell$ in the Boros-Moll polynomial $P_m(x)$. For a sequence $\{a_i\}_{i\geq 0}$, let $\mathcal{R}\{a_i\}_{i\geq 0}=\{a_{i+1}/a_i\}_{i\geq 0}$. A sequence is **infinitely log-monotonic** when every iterate has alternating log-concavity and log-convexity as specified by the paper's definition. **Infinite log-monotonicity conjecture.** The transposed Boros-Moll sequence $\{d_\ell(m)\}_{m\geq\ell}$ is infinitely log-monotonic for $\ell=0$. The sequence $\{d_\ell(m+1)/d_\ell(m)\}_{m\geq\ell}$ is infinite log-monotonic for each $\ell\geq 1$. The $ll=0$ sequence is known to be log-convex and ratio log-concave, but the asserted infinite behavior remains open.

candidates.title: Total positivity of bivariate forest polynomials
candidates.literal_statement: Let $f^\sharp_{n,k}(w)$ be the entries of the exponential Riordan array with generating function $G(t)=(e^{wT(t)}-1)/w$, where $T(t)$) is the tree function, and define $F_n^\sharp(x,w)=\sum_{k=0}^n f^\sharp_{n,k}(w)x^k$. A polynomial matrix is **coefficientwise totally positive** when all minors have coefficientwise nonnegative coefficients; a polynomial sequence is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive when all Hankel minors have coefficientwise nonnegative coefficients. **Total positivities for the bivariate forest polynomials.** (a) $F^\sharp=\bigl(f^\sharp_{n,k}(w)\bigr)_{n,k\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise totally positive in $w$. (b) ${\bm{F}}^\sharp=\bigl(F_n^\sharp(x,w)\bigr)_{n\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive in $x,w$. (c) ${\bm{F}}^{\sharp\triangle}=\bigl(f^\sharp_{n+1,1}(w)\bigr)_{n\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive in $w$. The source verifies parts (a) and (b) only to finite orders and notes that (c) follows from (b); no general proof is given.

candidates.title: Infinite log-concavity conjecture for the sparse-polynomial sequence
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $f_n(z)=f_{2,n}(z)$, and for a sequence $(a_n)$ define the operator

$$
\mathcal L(a_n)=a_n^2-a_{n-1}a_{n+1}.
$$

A sequence is called $k$-log-concave when $\mathcal L^j(a_n)\geq 0$ for $j=0,1,\ldots,k$, and **infinite log-concavity conjecture.** The sequence $(f_n(z))$ is $\infty$-log-concave for all $0\leq z\leq 1$. This is motivated by computations showing that repeated applications of $\mathcal L$ preserve nonnegative coefficients; the conjecture concerns all iterations and remains unresolved in the supplied source.

candidates.title: Unimodality conjecture for $\operatorname{LS}_{n,1}(112)$
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{LS}_{n,1}(112)$ be the generating polynomial under consideration for restricted growth functions of length $n$ containing the pattern $112$ exactly once; its coefficients form a finite sequence. **Unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial

$$
\operatorname{LS}_{n,1}(112)
$$

is unimodal. This conjecture concerns a refinement of the generating function whose symmetry is established in the surrounding results; its unimodality is not obtained from the standard product criterion because factors with internal zeros need not be unimodal.
candidates.proof_status: all-m algebraic equivalence, classical restricted cases and exact method obstruction only

candidates.title: Elementary symmetric-polynomial bounds for centered vectors and matrices
candidates.literal_statement: How sharply can elementary symmetric polynomials be bounded under vector or matrix centering constraints, and what quantitative consequences follow for permutation mixtures and finite exchangeability?

candidates.title: Unimodality of cycle-counting coefficients for functions
candidates.literal_statement: For $k,n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ with $0\le k\le n$, define $\left\{\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right\}$ to be the number of functions $f:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,n\}$ having exactly $k$ cycles, where a cycle is a connected component of the graph $\bigl\{\{x,f(x)\}\mid x\in\{1,\ldots,n\},\ x\ne f(x)\bigr\}$. Then the sequence $\left(\left\{\begin{smallmatrix}n\\0\end{smallmatrix}\right\},\ldots,\left\{\begin{smallmatrix}n\\n\end{smallmatrix}\right\}\right)$ is unimodal; the report states the stronger conclusion that it is ultra log-concave.

candidates.title: Ehrhart $h^\ast$-polynomial: Unimodality and Real-Rootedness (problem 20)
candidates.literal_statement:
A \textbf{spinal graph} $G$ is a connected digraph on vertex set $V=\{1,2,...,n\}$ with edge multiset $E$, where all edges are directed from smaller to larger vertices and $E$ contains all edges of the form $(i,i+1)$ for $i=1,\ldots,n-1$ (i.e., the “spine” of $G$).

What can be said about the $h^*$-polynomials of flow polytopes of spinal graphs?

\textbf{Conjecture:} descent polynomial of lower $G$-permutations $\leq h^*(\mathcal{F}_1;z) \leq $ descent polynomial of upper $G$-permutations, where $\leq$ indicates domination.

candidates.title: Brenti’s log-concavity conjecture for \widetilde{R}-polynomials
candidates.literal_statement:
**Conjecture 2 (Brenti).** Let $W$ be a finite Coxeter group. For $u,v\in W$ with $u\leq v$ in Bruhat order, define $\widetilde{R}_{u,v}$ by

$$q^{\ell(u,v)/2}\widetilde{R}_{u,v}(q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2})=R_{u,v}(q),$$

where $\ell(u,v)=\ell(v)-\ell(u)$. Since all powers of $q$ in $\widetilde{R}_{u,v}(q)$ have the same parity as $\ell(u,v)$, write

$$\widetilde{R}_{u,v}(q)=\begin{cases}Q_{u,v}(q^{2})&\text{if $\ell(u,v)$ is even},\\ qQ_{u,v}(q^{2})&\text{if $\ell(u,v)$ is odd},\end{cases}$$

with $Q_{u,v}(q)=\sum_i a_iq^i$. Then $Q_{u,v}$ is log-concave; that is, $a_i^2\geq a_{i-1}a_{i+1}$ for every applicable index $i$.

candidates.title: The totally stable matrix conjecture
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $f(x,y)=\sum f_i(x)y^i\in\mathbf{P}^{\mathrm{pos}}_2$, and form the upper-triangular coefficient matrix

$$
\varphi(f)(x,y)=
\begin{pmatrix}
f_0&f_1&f_2&\cdots\\
0&f_0&f_1&\cdots\\
0&0&f_0&\cdots\\
\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

A minor means the determinant of any finite square submatrix. **The totally stable matrix conjecture.** Every minor of $\varphi(f)(x,y)$ is a stable polynomial. The source describes this as being suggested by empirical evidence and does not prove it in general.
candidates.proof_status: prior public proof claim; not independently certified here

candidates.title: BSD regulator-quotient square conjecture for elliptic curves
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $E/K$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$, with a fixed invariant differential $\omega$. Let $L_i/K$ and $L'_j/K$ be finite extensions such that the associated permutation representations satisfy

$$
\bigoplus_i \operatorname{Ind}_{L_i/K} \mathbf{1}_{L_i}\simeq \bigoplus_j \operatorname{Ind}_{L'_j/K} \mathbf{1}_{L'_j}.
$$

Write $\operatorname{Reg}(E/L)$ for the regulator and $C(E/L)$ for the product of local Tamagawa and differential factors.

**BSD regulator-quotient square conjecture.** Then

$$
\prod_i \operatorname{Reg}(E/L_i)C(E/L_i)\equiv \prod_j \operatorname{Reg}(E/L'_j)C(E/L'_j)\pmod{\mathbb{Q}^{*2}}.
$$

This removes Tate–Shafarevich and torsion contributions by working modulo rational squares. It is presented as a consequence of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture and is open to the extent that the required BSD input is open.

candidates.title: Becker's conjecture on the Mahler classification of automatic real numbers
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $\xi$ be an irrational real number whose base-$b$ expansion is generated by a finite automaton; equivalently, its digit sequence is $k$-automatic for some integer base $k\geq 2$. In Mahler's classification, an $S$-number is a real number satisfying $0<w(\xi)<+\infty$, where

$$
w(\xi)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{w_n(\xi)}{n}
$$

and $w_n(\xi)$ is the supremum of the real numbers $\omega$ for which infinitely many integer polynomials $P(X)$ of degree at most $n$ satisfy $0<|P(\xi)|\leq H(P)^{-\omega}$. **Becker's conjecture.** Every irrational automatic real number is an $S$-number.
The conjecture asserts that irrational automatic real numbers share the generic Mahler classification of real numbers, since the set of $S$-numbers has full Lebesgue measure. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture is open or resolved.

candidates.title: Birationality criterion for residual linear type monomial ideals
candidates.literal_statement: Let $k[\mathbf{x}]=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and let $F$ be a finite set of $q\geq n$ monomials of the same degree $d\geq 2$. Suppose that the ideal $(F)\subset k[\mathbf{x}]$ is of **residual linear type**, meaning that the defining bihomogeneous ideal of its Rees algebra is generated in bidegrees $( *,1)$ and $(0,*)$. Let the **log-matrix** of $F$ record the exponents of its monomials, and let its **linear syzygy matrix** record the linear syzygies among the elements of $F$. Write $k[\mathbf{x}_d]$ for the $k$-subalgebra generated by all monomials of degree $d$. **Birationality criterion.** The following conditions are equivalent: (i) both the log-matrix and the linear syzygy matrix of $F$ have maximal rank; (ii) the extension $k[F]\subset k[\mathbf{x}_d]$ is birational. Ideals of residual linear type, also called ideals of fiber type, have defining relations generated by those of the symmetric algebra together with the polynomial relations over $k$. The conjecture asks whether the rank conditions on the monomial data and linear syzygies exactly characterize birationality for this class of ideals; its resolution is not supplied in the source.

candidates.title: Stabilization conjecture for kernels of monomial-induced maps
candidates.literal_statement: Let $R_n$ be the polynomial ring and let $Q_n$ denote the kernel considered above, with the symmetric group acting by permuting the indices. For a monomial $f$, consider the resulting sequence of kernels as $n$ varies. **Stabilization conjecture.** The sequence of kernels induced by a monomial $f$ stabilizes modulo the symmetric group. This conjecture generalizes the preceding finite-generation theorem, which establishes bounded-size generators for the relevant kernels but does not establish the asserted stabilization.

candidates.title: Lax's conjecture on determinantal representations of ternary hyperbolic polynomials
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a polynomial on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is hyperbolic of degree $d$ with respect to $e=(1,0,0)$ and satisfies $p(e)=1$. Let $I$ denote the $d\times d$ identity matrix and let $\mathbb{S}^d$ denote the space of real symmetric $d\times d$ matrices. **Lax's conjecture.** There exist matrices $B,C\in\mathbb{S}^d$ such that

$$
p(x,y,z)=\det(xI+yB+zC).
$$

The conjecture asserts that every normalized ternary hyperbolic polynomial has a definite symmetric determinantal representation, equivalently that its hyperbolicity cone is a semidefinite slice. The paper proves this conjecture, so the statement is now a theorem.

candidates.title: Abdesselam's log-concavity conjecture for subgroup-counting polynomials
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $g_\ell(n)$ denote the number of subgroups of index $n$ in $\mathbb{Z}^\ell$, and write

$$
P_n^{g_\ell}(X)=\sum_{k=0}^n p_n^{g_\ell}(k)X^k.
$$

Call a sequence $(a_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ **log-concave** at $k\geq 1$ when $a_k^2\geq a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$. **Abdesselam's conjecture.** For every $\ell,n\in\mathbb{N}$, the sequence $(p_n^{g_\ell}(k))_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ is log-concave at each $k\geq 1$. This generalizes the Heim–Neuhauser challenge, since $g_2=\sigma$; the source supplies no resolution status.

candidates.title: Sokal's Hankel-total positivity conjecture for GKP row-generating polynomials
candidates.literal_statement: Let $P_n(x;\bm{\mu})$ be the row-generating polynomials of the Graham–Knuth–Patashnik recurrence, with parameters $\bm{\mu}=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\alpha',\beta',\gamma')$ treated as indeterminates. Thus the coefficientwise partial order is taken in the seven variables $x,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\alpha',\beta',\gamma'$ on ${\mathbb Z}[x,\bm{\mu}]$. A sequence $(a_n)_{n\geq 0}$ is **Hankel-totally positive** when every minor of its Hankel matrix $(a_{i+j})_{i,j\geq 0}$ is nonnegative in this order. **Sokal's conjecture.** The sequence $(P_n(x;\bm{\mu}))_{n\geq 0}$ of row-generating polynomials of the GKP recurrence is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive, jointly in all seven indeterminates $x$ and $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\alpha',\beta',\gamma'$. This conjecture concerns total positivity of the Hankel matrix formed from the GKP row-generating polynomials and remains open.

candidates.title: The tree product conjecture for graphs of polynomial growth
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a finite graph, and write $f_H(r)$ for its growth function, namely the maximum number of vertices in a ball of radius $r$. For graphs $G_1,\dots,G_k$, let $G_1 \boxtimes \dots \boxtimes G_k$ denote their strong product, and let $K_m$ denote the complete graph on $m$ vertices. A graph class has degree-$d$ polynomial growth if its growth is bounded by $O(r^d)$. **The tree product conjecture.** There exist functions $g \colon \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $h \colon \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $c\in \mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 1}$ and $d \in \mathbb{N}$, every finite graph $H$ with growth $f_H(r)\leqslant cr^d$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of

$$
T_1 \boxtimes \dots \boxtimes T_d \boxtimes K_{g(c,d)},
$$

where each $T_i$ is a tree with growth $f_{T_i}(r)\leqslant h(c,d)r$. The conjecture seeks the tight number $d$ of product factors for graphs of degree-$d$ polynomial growth, with each factor a tree of linear growth and with a bounded clique factor; its resolution would strengthen the known product-structure theorem for graph classes of linear growth.

candidates.title: Partial flag Toeplitz limit conjecture
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $d4c3=(n_1,d4c5,n_k)$ be a finite strongly increasing sequence of positive integers, let $n_0=0$, and let $P_{d4c3}^{(n)}$ be the parabolic subgroup associated with the partial flag variety $SL_n/P_{d4c3}^{(n)}$. Consider a weakly decreasing sequence of $n_k$ non-negative real numbers $(d4c3_i)_{i=1}^{n_k}$ such that $d4c3_{n_i}>d4c3_{n_i+1}$ and $d4c3_j=d4c3_{j+1}$ otherwise. Let $u^{d4c4}d4d9\text{in}d4d9\operatorname{Toep}_{d4c4}(d4d9\mathbb R_{d4d9\ge 0})$ have generating function

$$
p_{u^{d4c4}}(x)=\frac{1}{\prod_{j=1}^{n_k}(1-d4c3_jx)}=\frac{1}{\prod_{i=1}^{k}(1-d4c3_{n_i}x)^{n_i-n_{i-1}}}.
$$

**Partial flag Toeplitz limit conjecture.** There exists a sequence $u^{(n)}d4d9\text{in}X_{P_{d4c3}^{(n)}}(\mathbb R_{>0})$ converging to $u^{d4c4}$; conversely, every infinite totally nonnegative Toeplitz matrix with a generating function of this form arises as such a limit. This proposes a precise description of limits of positive partial-flag varieties with fixed flag dimensions; the source provides no resolution evidence.

candidates.title: The Costas polynomial characterization conjecture for finite fields
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $q=p^n$ be a prime power and let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. A mapping $g$ has **fixed point** $0$ and a **cycle of length** $q-1$ if its permutation action contains the cycle consisting of all nonzero elements. An **orthomorphism** is a permutation $h$ of $\mathbb{F}_q$ such that $x\mapsto h(x)-x$ is also a permutation. A **linearized permutation polynomial** is a polynomial of the form $L(x)=\sum_i a_i x^{p^i}$ that permutes $\mathbb{F}_q$, and an element $\alpha\in\mathbb{F}_q$ is **primitive** if it generates the multiplicative group $\mathbb{F}_q^*$. **The Costas polynomial characterization conjecture.** The only mappings $g(x)$ with fixed point $0$ and a cycle of length $q-1$, and such that all compositions $g^k(x)$, for $1\leq k\leq q-2$, are orthomorphisms, are those of the form

$$
g(x)=L(\alpha L^{-1}(x)),
$$

where $L(x)$ is a linearized permutation polynomial and $\alpha$ is a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_q$. This is equivalent to the conjecture that the only Costas polynomials are of the form $L(x^s)$ with $\gcd(q-1,s)=1$. The preceding theorem supplies a lower bound by counting this family, but no resolution of the characterization is given here.

candidates.title: Shifted-binomial log-concavity conjecture for stable CSM–Schur coefficients
candidates.literal_statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition with parts at least $2$, and set

$$
c=\operatorname{codim}Y_\lambda=|\lambda|-\ell(\lambda).
$$

For every $f\ge c$, write the homogeneous degree-$f$ part of the stable Chern–Schwartz–MacPherson class as

$$
c^{SM}(Y_\lambda(d))_f=\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor f/2\rfloor}C_{\lambda,f,i}(d)s_{f-i,i}(a,b),
$$

where $C_{\lambda,f,i}(d)$ is polynomial in $d$ in the stable range. Define

$$
\widetilde C_{\lambda,f,i}(d)=(-1)^{f-c}C_{\lambda,f,i}(d),\qquad y=d-|\lambda|-2(f-c).
$$

**Shifted-binomial log-concavity conjecture.** The shifted polynomial

$$
\widetilde C_{\lambda,f,i}\bigl(y+|\lambda|+2(f-c)\bigr)
$$

has a nonnegative binomial-basis expansion

$$
\widetilde C_{\lambda,f,i}\bigl(y+|\lambda|+2(f-c)\bigr)=\sum_{j\ge0}\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j}\binom yj,
\qquad \gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j}\ge0.
$$

Moreover, after deleting possible initial zeroes, the coefficient sequence $(\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,0},\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,1},\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,2},\ldots)$ is log-concave:

$$
\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j}^{\,2}\ge\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j-1}\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j+1}.
$$
